title: Adaptive Intake: non-blocking compatibility metadata and rollback-safe pin policy
creator: Ava Ramirez
description:
Background: As community/open weights arrive with diverse packaging, runtime footprints, and implicit behavior differences, rigid 'must-pin-at-ingest' rules cause slow intake and block experimentation. We need an intake flow that allows non-blocking catalog registration with machine-readable compatibility metadata, automatic suggestion of a soft-pin policy, and a clear, automatable rollback path if runtime incompatibilities or quality regressions appear.

Goal: Define the product requirements and acceptance criteria for an adaptive intake flow that: (1) accepts model catalog entries with optional compatibility metadata without blocking ingestion, (2) assigns a default soft-pin policy that defers strict pinning until runtime probes and evals complete, and (3) exposes clear signals and automated rollback/fallback actions for runtime teams and customers.

Why now: Engineering capacity to run lightweight runtime probes and evals has increased; customers continue to request faster onboarding of experimental open variants; and current conservative pinning increases lead time for catalog availability. This PRD clarifies scope, trade-offs, and tests to enable a lower-friction intake while preserving safety and operational reliability.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog UI/API accepts model submissions with an optional 'compatibility_metadata' field (JSON string) and does not require 'pinned_version' at ingest time.
A 'soft_pin' default policy is assigned for unpinned entries and visible on the catalog entry page with a human-readable explanation.
Runtime probes (smoke-level inference checks) run automatically within 48 hours of ingest and write results to the entry's 'runtime_health' field.

An automated eval job executes a minimal quality regression check (based on a lightweight prompt set) and produces a pass/fail scorecard attached to the entry within 72 hours of ingest for community weights.

If runtime_health or eval scorecard fails threshold, the catalog entry transitions to 'quarantine' and all traffic is routed to a predefined fallback variant; rollback steps are recorded and actionable from the Console.
PM/Eng can mark an entry as 'pin_required' post-eval; pinning UI supports single-click pin and records the decision, date, and reason.
Documentation updated: intake API spec, recommended metadata schema, and operator playbook for quarantine and rollback are published in Confluence with links from the catalog UI.
E2E test exists that submits a synthetic model entry without pin, validates probes, triggers a simulated eval failure, and confirms Console shows quarantine state and fallback routing.
scope_inclusions: Intake API: add 'compatibility_metadata' optional field and a 'soft_pin' boolean flag defaulting true for unpinned community submissions.
Catalog UI: surface compatibility metadata, soft-pin status, runtime_health, and eval scorecard on model detail page.
Automated runtime probes: light inference/latency/kv-cache sanity checks (configurable) run on a best-effort basis.
Eval harness: lightweight prompt set (<=50 prompts) and a binary pass/fail gating rule for immediate intake acceptance.
Operator playbook and Confluence docs for quarantine handling and pin decision guidance.
scope_exclusions: Full-scale production-quality evals or large-scale A/B experiments (outside lightweight gating).
Automatic permanent pinning without human review.
Changes to tenant-level Dedicated / Private deployment policies (this is for catalog-only initial intake).
decisions: Non-blocking intake accepted: we will allow entries without a pinned version by default.
Soft-pin semantics: 'soft_pin' means entry is discoverable and routable to low-trust channels but excluded from high-SLA/enterprise routes until explicit pin.
Automated probes and evals are advisory but can flip state to 'quarantine' when failing critical thresholds; quarantine triggers automated fallback routing.
Quarantine is reversible: after remediation and re-run of probes/evals, entry can be moved back to active catalog without re-ingest.
dependencies: ENG-28941 (runtime-probes: lightweight probe runner and results API)
ENG-29450 (catalog-UI: model detail surface for runtime_health and evals)
ENG-30112 (routing: fallback routing for quarantined variants)
PM-732003 (eval-definition: define the 50-prompt lightweight gating set)
open_questions: What exact schema for 'compatibility_metadata' minimizes vendor lock-in but remains actionable? (e.g., fields: expected_seq_len, quantization_ok, kv_cache_behavior, recommended_batch_size)
Who signs off to move a quarantined community model back to active if evals were flaky due to transient infra failures? (SRE + PM or a designated reviewer?)
Should soft-pinned models be visible in public catalog listings or only in an 'experimental' filter?
What thresholds for 'runtime_health' and eval pass/fail minimize false positives while protecting customers?
notes: Trade-offs: faster intake increases catalog freshness but slightly raises operator visibility burden; automated quarantine reduces blast radius but requires robust fallback routing.
Security: community weights remain subject to standard PII/safety scanning; intake flow does not bypass content safety checks.
UX: keep the language non-technical on public pages; provide expandable 'dev details' for engineers/partners.
Rollout plan: start with 'experimental' catalog namespace for 30 days, monitor false positive quarantine rate, iterate thresholds before full catalog exposure.
